title: Add update and recovery audit records
description: Record sanitized update, migration, readiness, rollback, and recovery events in the existing audit trail.
acceptanceCriteria: Update/migration/rollback actions create audit records with actor/action/version/outcome/error category but no secrets
Records are created only after the relevant action outcome is known and survive pagination
Failed rollback/readiness events are queryable and distinguish attempted from completed actions
Authorization and rate limits apply to update/rollback endpoints if exposed through the API
Tests cover successful update, failed migration, failed readiness, rollback success/failure, and secret redaction

steps.description: Assert the expected audit actions/fields and absence of passwords/tokens/raw command lines for each recovery path.
steps.details: Suite scripts/test-release-audit.ts asserts the allowlist contract, the closed error-category set, version clipping, and that a raw error message is reduced to 'unknown'. No secret or command line is stored.

steps.description: Read audit helper, relevant update/settings routes, installer result handling, and current audit tests; identify the smallest integration point.
Record only allowlisted metadata and bounded error categories; preserve existing audit schema/indexes unless a migration is explicitly required.
steps.details: apps/web/src/lib/release-audit.ts builds details from a fixed key allowlist and stores only a bounded errorCategory. No schema change: the existing AuditLog table already has actorId/action/target/details/ip/createdAt. maintenance.ts now exempts retained release actions from the 90-day prune so lifecycle evidence survives. apps/web/app/api/settings/backup/route.ts records a release-audit event alongside the existing backup event.

steps.description: Run focused audit tests, pagination checks, custom harness, typecheck, and lint.
steps.details: npx tsx scripts/test-release-audit.ts -> 28 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, exit 0, against the real production build over HTTP. Proves unauthenticated 401, non-admin 403, per-user rate limit, the full ok/failed outcome matrix, actorId null for host-side actions, and a release record reachable past page 1 of the audit API. apps/web typecheck and targeted ESLint clean.

technicalNotes: Do not add a new audit table if the existing action metadata can represent the event; schema changes require separate migration evidence.
